editorial:
Imagine growing up in a small Michigan town where everyone knows your business and tradition is everything. You follow the story of Chad and his best friend Paul, who are just trying to navigate the awkwardness of being teenagers. The vibe is very grounded and raw, focusing on the scary moment when Paul decides to tell his parents he is gay. Since his parents are very conservative and old-school, the tension in the house builds up quickly, making you feel the stress of their reaction. It is a heavy story, but it feels real because it captures that fear of not being accepted by the people you love most.

What really works here is the acting, as the chemistry between the two leads makes you root for them. While the pacing slows down in the middle, the emotional payoffs are worth it. If you enjoy character studies that don't sugarcoat the truth, you will really appreciate this one. You can find it for rent on Apple TV if you want a quick watch, but it is definitely worth adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for those quiet movie nights. Just make sure you have some tissues ready because it gets pretty intense.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a heartbreaking but honest look at family bonds. After the blowout with his parents, Paul realizes that he cannot change their minds overnight. The final scenes show him finding strength in his friendship with Chad. While his parents do not fully accept him by the end, Paul learns to value his own truth over their approval. It ends on a hopeful note, showing that chosen family is sometimes more important than blood.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about friendship and family struggles.
